question.problem: Consider the linear transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x-2y+z \\ 6x-3y-3z \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ Find $\,\text{Ker}(T).$
question.worked_solution:
Finding the kernel of $T$ is equivalent to finding the null space of the standard matrix of $T.$

Fror the given linear transformation, the standard matrix is $T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 6 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].$

Setting $x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],$ we then need to solve the equation $Tx=0.$ First, we find reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 6 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 9 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{9}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$ and $y$, and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$

From the second equation, we get $y=z.$ Substituting these into the first equation, we have 

$$
x=2y-z=2z-z=z.
$$

Therefore, the kernel of the linear transformation $\,T$ is $\{[\begin{aligned}z \\ z \\ z\end{aligned}]\,:\,z\in R\}.$
